Libya imposes nationwide curbs as dengue outbreak disrupts economic activity

TRIPOLI, June 17 – Libya enforced sweeping closures of schools, businesses, and public venues on Monday as a dengue fever outbreak intensified, dealing a fresh blow to the country’s fragile economy and stretching utilities and public services.

The Ministry of Health reported 2,400 confirmed cases and nine deaths since the start of the month, with cases recorded in major cities including Tripoli, Benghazi, and Misrata. All non-essential businesses, markets, and government offices have been ordered shut for an initial two-week period, while movement between cities is heavily restricted.

The General Electricity Co of Libya, which supplies power nationwide, said it was forced to scale back operations after a number of staff were instructed to quarantine following suspected exposure to the virus. “Our teams are working under severe constraints, and some routine maintenance is delayed,” company spokesman Khaled al-Mansouri told local media, warning of possible interruptions in service.

The closures have disrupted logistics networks and halted much of the retail and service sectors. “Dengue is not just a health emergency—it’s paralyzing daily life and business. Libya’s recovery from years of conflict is at risk,” said Samir El-Haddad, an economist at the Libyan Chamber of Commerce. He estimated lost output could already exceed $30 million since the outbreak began.

Authorities have urged citizens to remain indoors and are intensifying mosquito control programs. The National Trade Federation called for urgent government support for affected workers and small businesses.

Health officials said the restrictions would remain under review as they monitor the outbreak’s progression.
